note: Wonders done (16, verified vs namu_wonders new-edition values; Internet formula and Transcontinental Railroad doubling confirmed via faq_v15.pdf + fandom wiki). Leaders done (24: 6 per age A/I/II/III, from namu_heroes.txt new-edition values; base-24 roster cross-checked vs fandom_card_list_digital.json; six unchanged-from-2006 leaders and Sid Meier confirmed via throughtheages.fandom.com — OPEN_QUESTIONS items 3-4 resolved).

cards.name: Pyramids
cards.text: +1 civil action.

cards.name: Hanging Gardens
cards.text: +1 culture production, +2 happy faces.

cards.name: Colossus
cards.text: +2 strength, +1 to colonization bids.

cards.name: Library of Alexandria
cards.text: +1 culture, +1 science production; civil and military hand limits +1.

cards.name: Great Wall
cards.text: +1 culture, +1 happy face, each infantry and artillery unit gains +1 strength.

cards.name: St. Peter's Basilica
cards.text: +2 culture, +1 happy face; every building/card providing happy faces provides one additional happy face.

cards.name: Universitas Carolina
cards.text: +1 culture, +2 science production.

cards.name: Taj Mahal
cards.text: +3 culture production, +1 blue token. If you replaced your leader this turn, taking this wonder costs you 2 civil actions less. (2015 only -- the 2006 card printed just the culture. Take-discount clause transcribed verbatim from Board Game Arena's implementation, sources/bga_throughtheages_material.inc.php card id 98, and corroborated by sources/namu_wonders.txt's new-edition entry; independently confirmed against 317 real BGO human takes, see docs/REPLAY.md's seventh pass.)

cards.name: Transcontinental Railroad
cards.text: +4 strength; one of your best mines produces twice as many resources. (2015: stages 3-3-3-3, strength +4. Doubling CONFIRMED retained by FAQ v1.5 p.9: doubles the production of one worker on the best mine technology card that has workers; labs affected by Bill Gates are not mines; benefit counts toward Impact of Industry.)

cards.name: Eiffel Tower
cards.text: +4 culture production, +1 happy face.

cards.name: Kremlin
cards.text: +2 culture, +1 civil action, +1 military action, -1 happy face (2015 values).

cards.name: Ocean Liners
cards.text: Once per turn you may increase population without spending a civil action or food (2015).

cards.name: First Space Flight
cards.text: When completed, gain culture equal to the sum of levels of all technologies you have developed.

cards.name: Fast Food Chains
cards.text: When completed, gain 2 culture per worker on farms and mines and 1 per worker on urban/military technologies.

cards.name: Internet

effects.onBuildCulture: sum over urban buildings of (culture + science + strength) they give, including leader modifications to those buildings' output

cards.text: When completed, immediately score culture equal to the combined culture, science, and strength your urban buildings give. (CONFIRMED via fandom wiki + FAQ v1.5: leader effects on urban-building output count — Sid Meier, Shakespeare, Bach, Chaplin, Newton, Einstein.)

cards.name: Hollywood
cards.text: When completed, gain culture equal to twice the total culture production of your theaters and libraries (2015).

cards.name: Aristotle
cards.text: Every time you take a technology card from the card row, you score 1 science point. (2015 unchanged from 2006; CONFIRMED via fandom wiki.)

cards.name: Alexander the Great
cards.text: Each of your military units has +1 strength. As a political action, you may remove Alexander from the game to take 1 yellow token from the box into your yellow bank. (2015)

cards.name: Julius Caesar
cards.text: +1 strength; +1 military action. Once per game, you may take two political actions in your politics phase. (2015)

cards.name: Hammurabi
cards.text: On your turn, you may use one military action as a civil action. When you take a new leader from the card row, it costs 1 less civil action. (2015)

cards.name: Homer
cards.text: +1 happy face. When you build or upgrade a military unit on your turn, gain 1 resource. When replacing Homer, you may place him under one of your completed wonders; that wonder provides +1 happy face. (2015)

cards.name: Moses
cards.text: Increasing your population costs you 1 food less. (2015 unchanged from 2006; CONFIRMED via fandom wiki.)

cards.name: Leonardo da Vinci
cards.text: Your best lab or library produces extra science: +1 per level. When you play a technology card, produce 1 resource. (2015 unchanged from 2006; CONFIRMED via fandom wiki.)

cards.name: Christopher Columbus
cards.text: As a political action, you may remove Columbus from the game to colonize a territory card from your hand without sacrificing any military units. (2015; 2006 was once-per-game without removal.)

cards.name: Frederick Barbarossa
cards.text: By spending 1 military action, you may increase population and build a military unit all at once; the population increase costs 1 less food and the unit costs 1 less resource. (2015; 2006 used a civil action.)

cards.name: Genghis Khan
cards.text: You may treat any of your infantry units as cavalry units to form armies matching your tactic. At the end of your turn, if you are one of the two strongest civilizations (ties in your favor), gain 3 culture points. (2015)

cards.name: Joan of Arc
cards.text: +1 culture production; +1 military action. +1 strength for each happy face provided by your temples and your government. When you begin your politics phase, you may look at the top card of the current events deck. (2015)

cards.name: Michelangelo
cards.text: Each production phase, produce 1 culture for each happy face provided by your temples, theaters, and completed wonders. When you take a wonder card from the card row, you spend no additional civil actions even if you have completed wonders. (2015)

cards.name: James Cook
cards.text: When colonizing, you may discard up to 2 military cards, gaining +1 colony bonus for each card discarded. Each production phase, your first colony produces 2 extra culture and each additional colony produces 1 culture. (2015; nerfed from 2006's 2 per colony.)

cards.name: Isaac Newton
cards.text: Your best lab or library produces extra science equal to its level. Every time you play a technology card, get 1 spent civil action back. (2015 unchanged from 2006; CONFIRMED via fandom wiki.)

cards.name: J. S. Bach
cards.text: Each production phase, produce 1 culture for each theater you have. Developing theater technologies costs 2 less science. Once per turn, as a civil action, you may upgrade one of your urban buildings to a theater of the same or higher level, paying the resource cost difference as normal. (2015)

cards.name: Maximilien Robespierre
cards.text: +1 military action. When you declare a revolution, you spend all your military actions instead of all your civil actions. When you declare a revolution, gain 3 culture points. (2015)

cards.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
cards.text: +2 military actions. +2 strength for each type of military unit you have (infantry, cavalry, artillery, air forces). (2015)

cards.name: William Shakespeare
cards.text: +1 happy face. If you have a library, building a theater costs 1 less resource and developing a theater technology costs 1 less science; if you have a theater, the same discounts apply to your libraries. Each production phase, produce 2 culture for each pair of one library and one theater. (2015)

cards.name: Albert Einstein
cards.text: Your best lab or library produces extra science: 1 per level. Score 3 culture when you play a technology card. (2015 unchanged from 2006; CONFIRMED via fandom wiki.)

cards.name: Bill Gates
cards.text: Each production phase, each of your labs produces resources equal to its level (stored as on a mine; not affected by Transcontinental Railroad or Event: Industry). When Bill Gates is removed from the game or the game ends, gain culture equal to that extra resource production. (2015; 2006 Tesla penalty clause on other players removed.)

cards.name: Charlie Chaplin
cards.text: +2 happy faces. Your best theater produces double culture each production phase. (2015 rename of Rock'n'Roll Icon; ability unchanged per namu.)

cards.name: Mahatma Gandhi
cards.text: +2 culture production. You may not play aggression or war cards. Opponents pay twice the military actions to play aggressions or wars against you. (2015 unchanged from 2006; CONFIRMED via fandom wiki — the expansion, not the base game, changed it to +3 military actions.)

cards.name: Sid Meier
cards.text: Each of your labs produces culture: 1 per level; each lab produces 1 less science. (2015; CONFIRMED same mechanic as 2006 Alex Randolph via fandom wiki, and by FAQ v1.5 example: two Age-III Computers workers produce a combined 8 science and 6 culture per turn. FAQ: his ability also affects the Internet wonder score.)

cards.name: Winston Churchill
cards.text: Once each turn, choose one: gain 3 culture points; or gain 3 science points usable only to develop military unit technologies and 3 resources usable only to build or upgrade military units. (2015; completely reworked from 2006.)
